justification: B packs the same content into two pages: a strong green cover band carries the title, followed directly by the summary and position statement. Gold rules separate the sections, so the reading rhythm stays steady. A spends a whole page on a sparse cover and leaves a large empty area at the bottom of A3. A's numbered headings are a little clearer, and its chart is slightly taller. Overall, B's density and banding feel more finished.

B offers a consistent teal palette, running headers, a table of contents (B2), a section divider page (B5), and a teal-accented table and charts (B4, B6, B7) that give clear structure. A crams section headings at the bottoms of chart pages (A3, A4), leaving orphaned section starts and a mostly empty final page (A5). A's serif Arabic is elegant, but B's overall hierarchy and rhythm are stronger.

A keeps a consistent sans type with numbered headings, running headers and contained figures. Its KPI row on A2 is clear, and the table on A5 is ruled. B has the stronger full-bleed cover image on B1, but its body type is small and uneven. Its KPI row on B2 loses the percent signs and colour cues. The section on B4 runs over from the previous page, and the bleeding images there crowd the text.

The two designs share the same layout. A uses a naskh-style Arabic face that reads more comfortably in body text than B's geometric Kufi-style face. A's running header also shows the title, giving clear wayfinding. A gives the Prevention section its own page with a rule and an intro. B squeezes that section's heading and intro onto the bottom of the waiting-times page, so the section opener feels cramped and the rhythm suffers. B's numerals in its display face also read less naturally.

Design A strands its freight chart alone at the top of an otherwise empty page (A3) and leaves the short appendix table almost alone on a final page (A7). Its callout box covers part of the illustrations (A4, A5). Design B fits the same content into five well-filled pages. The chart sits with its stats (B2), the callouts sit beside the images rather than over them (B3, B4), and the appendix joins the financial review (B5). A's serif text and headings are more refined, and B's heavy header and footer bands are a little crowded, but A's layout gaps outweigh this.

A fits the content into four well-paced pages with an illustrated cover, images paired with text, and captions kept together. B separates a caption ('أرشيف البلدية') from its image across pages B3–B4, mixes body text sizes, and leaves an orphaned image alone on a nearly empty final page B5. Its plain cover B1 is also less engaging.

B is the more designed, coherent report. It has a full-bleed image cover, consistent teal section bands, a highlighted pull quote, and a shaded current-year column in the table. A is cleaner and more legible, with larger, consistent sans type. A's KPI numbers on A2 are bold and clear, while B2 loses the percent signs (92, 11). B's text is smaller and uses a mixed serif. B's governance appendix heading on B5 is also weak, styled like body text. Overall, B's structure and visual identity outweigh these flaws.

A has a cohesive full-bleed cover, consistent serif typography with branded orange rules and a running header, and section-divider pages that act as navigation. These dividers are sparse, though, and A appears to omit the governance appendix. B is more compact and includes the appendix, but its body text is letter-spaced and hangs indented under outdented sans headings, and its cover splits awkwardly into image and white. Its black caption boxes and charts also feel less integrated. On balance A reads as the more polished report.

A's last page is an orphaned image floating in a nearly empty page. A4 also opens with a stray 'أرشيف البلدية' credit that has been cut off from its figure, and the pull quote sits awkwardly between them. B uses four pages instead of five, and its pages are fuller. In B, the final garden image is paired with the closing text (B4), and the figures sit with their sections. B3 has a pull quote stranded at the page bottom with its continuation on B4, but the flow is still more even overall.

B opens on a full-bleed illustrated cover with a clear title, gives the chairman's quote a strong pull-quote treatment, and keeps the key figures beneath their own heading. Its sections are spaced consistently across pages. In A the cover band and the opening text share one page, the figures band sits detached at the top of page 2 under the wrong section, and the quote is understated. A's text is slightly denser and larger, which helps typography a little. Overall, B is more polished.

B uses a larger, clearer Arabic sans with stronger section headings and gold rules. It adds a running header band on page 2 and uses a brand-coloured chart that matches the palette. A's serif face is refined, but its body and heading text is small and light. A's chart uses an off-palette black bar, and its KPI '24' lacks a % sign. A's annex heading is also weak.

B uses a more readable Naskh-style body face and a fuller running header and footer. Its Prevention section opens on its own page (B7) with its charts, and the table of contents is accurate. A squeezes the Prevention heading in under the table on A6, leaving it split from its charts on A7. A also uses a geometric Kufi face with wide justified spacing, which reads less smoothly.

B uses a more refined Naskh-style text face with comfortable line spacing, which reads better than A's heavy, justified geometric sans with stretched word gaps. B's taller chart fills page 2 better, leaving less dead space at the bottom than A2. A's two-line title is bolder, but B overall feels calmer and more balanced.

A keeps the freight chart with its section on A3, so pages stay full and evenly paced. B pushes the chart onto a nearly empty B4, leaving a large void. B also has inconsistent body sizes, with larger lead paragraphs beside smaller dense text on B3 and B6. A's sans headings with numbered sections give a clearer hierarchy and a consistent header and footer band. B's cover and pull quote are more refined, but the orphaned chart page and uneven text sizing outweigh that.

B sets the title over the full-bleed cover art, and its gold rules and running header tie the pages together. Its images sit within the text margins, its tables have clear rules, and its percentage signs are present. A has full-bleed images that break the margins (A3, A4), section text that runs over awkwardly onto A4, rule-light tables (A5) and missing % signs in the key figures (A2).

A uses a clearer sans with stronger header/footer bands carrying section running heads. It also gives the Prevention section its own page with its charts. B splits Prevention across B6 (heading and text crammed under the table) and B7 (charts alone), which breaks rhythm. B adds a TOC page (B2) with Latin page numbers and a lot of empty space. B's lighter, thinner Arabic face and tiny footers read weaker.

B packs the same content into two well-filled pages with a running header band and an even rhythm of sections. A leaves its cover page more than half empty below the KPIs, and its last page holds only a chart and a short note above a large void. A's title breaks awkwardly onto a second line with a single word, whereas B's title wraps cleanly. B's summary block is slightly cramped, but overall its pages are better balanced.

A uses a clean sans Arabic face with a teal/navy palette, a header band with logo, a contents page and a section divider for 'جودة الخدمة'. These give clear structure and consistent page rhythm. B is monochrome and more austere. Its section headings sit in the middle of pages (B3, B4), and the full-width rules overshoot the margins. Its small serif body text is less consistent with the charts. A has a nearly empty divider page and some sparse pages, but its identity and hierarchy are stronger overall.

A's cover carries an illustrated scene above a green title band. B's cover is an almost empty dark page. A's interiors have a consistent running header and footer and pair the pull quotes with images side by side. B overlays dark quote boxes on the images, hiding much of the artwork. B also mixes body text sizes from paragraph to paragraph, so its rhythm is uneven.

Design A leaves the bottom half of the cover page empty and the bottom of page 3 empty, so content is spread thinly across three pages. Design B fits the same content into two well-filled pages: the summary and balance sheet sit on page 1, and the income statement, chart and notes sit on page 2. Both designs share the same flaws: the chart title is reversed and the percent signs are missing or broken.

B's section-divider pages hold only a heading and a tab list, which wastes whole spreads (B2, B5). Only some sections get dividers: the Chair's letter and North quay do, while People and Environment do not. That breaks the rhythm. B's cover title also wraps awkwardly ('Annual / Report 2025') and sits low over the artwork (B1). A runs straight from section to section with consistent sans headings and a clean cover (A1, A2, A4). B's appendix is missing from the shown pages. Charts and tables are near-identical in both, and B's orange rules and header band are pleasant. Even so, A reads more efficiently.

A packs the content into four well-filled pages with consistent headers, section rules and figures integrated beside text. B spreads the same content over seven pages. Its pages are mostly empty: B3 and B4 have large blank lower halves, and B7 is an orphaned image floating alone. The chapter dividers (B2, B5) feel heavy for such short sections, and the pull quote on B6 is weakened into small indented text.

A uses an elegant serif and a refined cover, but it wastes pages. A2 and A5 are near-empty divider pages, and A4 holds a lone chart with about two-thirds of the page blank. The governance appendix appears only as a tab and its content is missing. B fits the same content into five dense, balanced pages: the chart sits under the stats on B2, and the image and pull-quote panels align cleanly on B3–B4. B5 also includes the governance table. Its header and footer bands give consistent navigation.

A uses a strong teal cover band and an anchored KPI band, so the cover and figures feel designed. B's cover is a mostly empty white page. B's KPI row is weak: '98 million m³' wraps awkwardly and the numbers float without structure. B also leaves large empty areas at the bottom of pages. A's tables carry a highlighted 2025 column, while B's tables are plainer. A does have a split KPI block at the top of A2, but overall its pages are denser and more balanced.

Both designs share the same layouts and charts. A sets its body text in a calmer naskh-style face with comfortable line spacing, and it includes a table of contents (A2). B uses a heavier geometric face with tighter leading. B's justified paragraphs leave stretched gaps (B3) and its table caption sits cramped under the text (B5). B's full-width header and footer bands are stronger, but its typography reads less comfortably.

B's full-bleed illustrated cover and the consistent gold rule with logo header give it a stronger, more finished identity. Its pull quote is a real typographic moment, and the KPI row with rules sits cleanly. A's cover is sparse, and its KPI numbers wrap awkwardly, with 'مليون م³' breaking onto a second line. A does keep numbered headings, which give slightly clearer hierarchy, and A's text face is a touch more legible. Tables are near-identical.

B adds a contents page, a section divider, header and footer bands, and numbered headings, which give clearer structure. Its accent colour unifies the charts and table, and its table rules are tidier. A's Naskh type is elegant, but its sections run together with weak separation, and its axis labels are illegible. B's ToC mixes Latin and Arabic numerals, but it is still the stronger document overall.

A keeps the year-in-numbers stats and freight chart together on one page (A3). B strands the chart alone on a mostly empty page (B3). B's headings hang outside the text column. B also mixes oversized lead paragraphs with small body text inconsistently (B2, B4, B5). A's divider pages are sparse (A2, A4), but its header/footer bands and consistent colour give coherent structure. B's chapter tagging is only a thin running footer.

A uses a cleaner Arabic sans with gold section rules echoing the green banner, keeps the % sign on the 24% metric (B shows a bare "24"), and adds running headers and footers on page 2. Its chart is tinted green to match the brand, whereas B's chart is black and grey and feels disconnected. B's naskh-style body is legible but smaller and less consistent with its sans numerals. Both share the mirrored chart title.

Design A has an illustrated cover, clear chapter divider pages with a navigation strip, and a consistent header and footer, which gives it a strong structure. Its main weaknesses are sparse pages, including a mostly empty A3 and an orphan image on A7. Design B is more compact, but its cover is a plain dark field. B3 crams two sections together, and its body text wraps unevenly around the figure. On B4 a caption is orphaned at the top of the page, and a pull quote is styled like a heading, which confuses the hierarchy. B5 also ends on a lone image. Overall, A reads as the more polished document.

A fits the content on two well-filled pages: the cover band, KPIs and balance sheet share page 1, and the income table, chart and notes share page 2. B spreads the same material over three pages. Its first page is half empty under the KPIs, and its last page holds only the chart and a short note above a large blank area. B's title also breaks awkwardly, leaving one orphan word on the second line. A has a running header band that aids navigation. Both share the chart's reversed-title glitch.

A has a table of contents (A2), but its 'الوقاية' section is stranded at the bottom of A6 under the table, splitting the section from its charts on A7. B keeps the Prevention intro with its charts on B6, and its running header/footer bands give consistent navigation. A's text sits more cramped, and its stat numerals on A3 use odd glyphs (٨٤٪ rendered oddly). B reads more coherently overall.

A has a strong illustrated cover and consistent teal section bands, a prominent pull quote, and stat cards with rules, giving clear hierarchy and rhythm. B has a bare cover with a lone logo. Its headings are small and plain, its pull quote is weak, and its stats break awkwardly, with 'مليون م³' wrapping to a second line. B's text is slightly cleaner, but A's structure and imagery are better.

B is the more consistent and polished design, despite a weaker cover. Its typeface is uniform, its section rules and running header bands are clear, and its stats panel is coloured. Its tables have a highlighted current-year column and stronger rules (B2, B4). A has a stronger cover image and an elegant pull quote (A1, A2), but its body text sizes are inconsistent and its stats row floats loosely (A2). Its full-bleed images leave awkward partial pages (A3, A4), and its financial table is faint (A5). B's weaknesses are a cramped cover and a stats panel separated from its heading across a page break (B1, B2).

A packs the content into two well-filled pages. A green title band opens the document and gold rules divide the sections. B spends a whole page on a sparse centered cover. That leaves B's page 2 with a large empty lower half. Its numbered headings are slightly clearer, but the pages feel padded. The tables and chart are essentially identical in both.

A opens with a strong dark title band, but most of page A1 is left empty below the KPIs. The appendix heading on A3 is the same size as body text, and A3 ends mostly blank. B uses a sparse cover, then fills B2 and B3 evenly. The chart sits beside the income table, and the numbered headings are clear. Text justification in B also avoids the stretched line seen in A2's income paragraph. Both share the same reversed chart title.

A treats the closing statement as a large green pull quote under an orange rule, which gives page 3 a clear emphasis. Its image on A3 wraps the text beside it. B shrinks that quote to an indented line that looks like a stray paragraph (B3). B also stacks the small building image above its text, leaving an awkward empty space beside it. B's dark green header and footer bands are tidy, but its last page is more than half empty (B4). A's Naskh-style text face reads more comfortably.

A fits the content into 5 well-filled pages. The freight chart sits with the year-in-numbers figures, and the governance appendix shares the finance page. B strands the freight chart alone on a nearly empty page (B3) and the governance table on another (B7), leaving large voids. B's callout boxes overlay and obscure the illustrations (B4, B5), whereas A places text panels beside the images. B's hanging headings with indented body text give a less consistent rhythm, while A's teal header and footer bands and consistent sans styling feel more cohesive.

Design A's cover is plain, and the caption "أرشيف البلدية" is orphaned at the top of A4. A5 holds only a stranded image on a mostly empty page. In A2 and A3 the quote boxes sit over the illustrations and obscure them. Design B has a strong illustrated cover. It sets its quote panels beside the images instead of over them. Running header and footer bands frame each page, and the final image is paired with its text on B4. B's weak point is the pull quote on B3, which is shrunk to near body size and loses the emphasis it has in A4.

A opens with a full illustrated cover and gives each section its own page under a strong teal band, with a prominent pull quote and an open key-figures row. B packs the cover title, chairman's letter and key-figures heading onto page 1. B also strands the KPI box at the top of page 2, away from its heading on B1, which breaks the flow. B's sans type reads cleanly, but A's structure and pacing are more polished.

A applies a consistent teal palette, running headers with a logo, a table of contents, and a section-divider page, which gives a clear structure. Its sans Arabic body type also reads cleanly. B is more compact, but sections sit crammed at page bottoms. Its headings hang flush past the margin on B3 and B4, its type is a lower-contrast serif, and the % sign is missing on the 84 figure (B2). Its grey and black charts are flatter, and the last page is half empty.

B uses a refined Naskh-style Arabic face with generous line spacing, which reads more comfortably than A's geometric sans set tighter and justified with wide gaps (A3). B adds a contents page (B2), and its table rows are airier (B6). Its light header with a rule is less heavy than A's dark bars on every page. A's heavy bars and denser text give it a cruder feel.

B uses a cleaner, more legible Arabic sans with numbered section headings, consistent running headers and footers, and a chart coloured in the document's green. A's appendix heading is undersized relative to the other sections, its chart uses a mismatched black bar, and its folio appears only on page 2. A's green title band is striking. B's sparse cover is elegant, though somewhat empty. Overall B reads as more polished and consistent.

Design B breaks the caption from its source: the line 'أرشيف البلدية' is orphaned at the top of B4. The final image is stranded alone on B5, which is otherwise empty. B2 also leaves a large blank bottom. Design A keeps images with their captions and sections, and fits the content into four pages that flow coherently. A's page 3 also uses a dangling side image and has some unevenness, but its pacing is overall tighter.

B is more polished. It adds a table of contents, a consistent teal header rule and logo, a section divider page, and coordinated navy chart accents. Its Arabic sans typography is crisp, with larger headings. A crams sections together, such as the Service Quality heading squeezed at the bottom of A3, and its black-and-grey palette is plainer. B's left-aligned key-figure block has some empty space, but its overall rhythm and branding are stronger.

A uses a calmer Naskh-style face with comfortable margins. Its taller chart reads clearly, and page 2 is evenly filled. B's geometric font is heavier and its justified body text shows stretched word gaps. B's squat chart leaves a large empty area at the bottom of page 2. Both chart titles render reversed. B's dark header band is a plus, but overall A is more refined.

A has an illustrated cover and steady body text set at one size throughout. Its pull-quote panels sit cleanly beside the images. Its header and footer bands frame each page consistently. B's cover is a mostly empty dark field. B also mixes body text sizes inconsistently (B2, B3, B4). Its quote boxes overlay the images, and the section text is orphaned at the top of B4. A's last page is underfilled, but overall it reads more coherently.

The layouts are nearly identical. A uses heavy dark header and footer bands, and its section numbering is inconsistent: Western '1', '2' sits beside Arabic-Indic '٣' in the contents (A2) and headings (A3, A5, A7). B uses light running heads with a thin rule and centred folios, and its unnumbered headings avoid the mixed-digit problem (B2, B6, B7). B's Naskh-style text face reads well. A's chapter numeral '2' on A5 adds a little emphasis, but overall B is cleaner and more consistent.

B carries the green brand into its rules, table borders and the 2025 bar, with gold section dividers and a running header, so the pages hang together better. B also keeps the % signs on the KPIs, which A drops ("٢٤" alone). A's naskh face looks more traditional, but its chart uses a black highlight that clashes with the green cover. Both share the same broken chart title.

A runs the content compactly over 5 pages with consistent section heads, and the Chair's letter keeps its heading. B adds two near-empty divider pages (B2, B4), while sections 2, 4, 5 and 6 get no divider, so the rhythm is uneven. B's running header on B3 reads "The year in numbers" while the Chair's letter runs first. B8 is a mostly empty page holding one small table. B's serif body text is pleasant, but the structural inconsistencies outweigh it.

A uses a softer Arabic face with numbered headings (1.1, 2.1) and solid header/footer bands carrying running section titles, which make navigation clear. B's geometric font is stiffer and its justified body text opens wide gaps (B4, B7). B also squeezes the Prevention section opener onto the bottom of the waiting-time page (B6), which weakens the section rhythm. A gives Prevention its own page (A7).

B is the stronger design. Its consistent header and footer bands and its blue accent palette in the charts and table give it a coherent identity. A section divider page (B4) clarifies the structure. Section headings in B open at the top of pages, while A crams the "جودة الخدمة" and "الوقاية" headings into page bottoms (A3, A4) and leaves weak section breaks. A's naskh typeface is elegant, but its small text and grey charts feel drabber. B's divider page is somewhat sparse and has a stray rule, but overall it reads more clearly.

A uses a consistent sans Arabic face with a larger, two-line title and gold section rules. Its KPI figures read clearly, with the percent sign kept on the 24% figure. The header band on page 2 and a chart in the brand colours make it feel cohesive. B's small naskh body text is fainter. B drops the percent sign from the 24 figure. B's chart uses an off-brand black and grey palette, and its section headings look weaker.

A keeps the chart with its income statement and introduces each section with a numbered, larger heading, so the hierarchy is clear. Its headers and footers give consistent navigation. B's section headings are small and weak, close in size to body text. Its cover title wraps awkwardly, leaving 'الوفاء' alone on a second line. B also separates the chart from the income table onto a mostly empty last page, and its justified text has uneven word gaps. Both share the reversed chart title.

B is the stronger design. It keeps the freight chart together with the numbers section on B3, while A strands that chart alone on a mostly empty page (A4). B also includes the governance appendix (B8), which A omits even though its contents list promises it. B's running header and footer bands help navigation. A has a more elegant serif treatment and a large pull quote on A3, but its weaker page flow outweighs that. B's justified text shows some rivers.

A fits the content onto two well-filled pages. The balance sheet sits under the summary on A1, and the income table, chart and notes follow on A2. B leaves the lower half of B1 empty and spills the chart onto B3, which is mostly blank. B also wraps its title onto two lines, and its justified paragraph on B2 shows stretched word gaps. The tables are styled alike in both designs.

A opens with a full-bleed illustrated cover and gives the chairman's quote prominent pull-quote treatment. Its key figures sit in a clean, aligned stat row with rules above them, and gold accent bands run consistently across the pages. B's cover is mostly empty white space. B's key-figures block breaks "٩٨ مليون م³" across two lines and leaves the large lower part of B2 empty. B's quote is also weak, set as an indented line. Both designs have equivalent tables and inner pages.

A has a striking illustrated cover, clear chapter divider pages with a navigation sidebar, and consistent header and footer bands. On A3 and A6, the image and pull-quote panels sit side by side and read cleanly. A wastes space: A3 and A4 are mostly empty, and A7 holds only a lone image. B is compact but plain. Its cover (B1) is a flat dark page. Its section heads are weak and small. The text overlays on the images in B2 and B3 are heavy. The body text is small and inconsistently sized and justified, with loose word spacing on B3 and B4. The page-number fonts in B's footers are also inconsistent.

A keeps a consistent page system: a coloured title band, a running header, gold rules, a highlighted KPI band, and a table with a shaded current-year column. Its body text is larger and more legible. B has a strong full-bleed cover image (B1). But its small body type, sparse KPI row and unshaded tables (B2, B5) feel thinner. B also has awkward breaks, such as section text spilling onto the next page in B4, and large empty areas in B3 and B5.

A includes a table of contents and numbered section headings with a large section numeral on the divider page, which give clearer navigation and hierarchy. Its body text is set ragged with comfortable leading. B justifies its Arabic body text, producing uneven word gaps (B3, B6), and its table caption sits cramped against the paragraph above (B5). A's TOC mixes Latin and Arabic numerals, which is a minor flaw.

B keeps the freight chart with its numbers on B3, so it avoids A's nearly empty chart page (A3). Its callout panels sit beside the images and are easier to read than A's dark overlays covering the artwork (A4, A5). The B2/B4 divider pages with a section index give clear navigation. The header and footer bands frame each page consistently. A's pull quote and hanging-indent layout is elegant, but the A3 gap breaks its rhythm. B's divider pages add some bulk, though.

A uses a clean, consistent Arabic sans with numbered section heads and running headers. Its key figures are clearer, keeping the % sign on 24% (A2). B's green cover band is striking, but its body text is small and cramped. B also drops the % sign and the section numbering, its headings are weaker (B1, B2), and its chart turns to black and grey. Both share the same reversed chart title.

B has a proper split-image cover, consistent full-width section bands, a prominent pull quote, and a clean KPI row, which give a clear, steady rhythm. A crams the cover, letter and highlights onto one page. Its KPI box is then orphaned at the top of page 2, away from its heading. A's body text is larger and darker, but its pages feel uneven. B drops the % signs in its KPIs and has small body text, yet overall it reads as the more polished report.

B has a striking full-bleed cover, chapter divider pages with a tab-style index, and coloured header and footer bands. But its pacing breaks down. B3 and B4 are mostly empty, and B7 holds only a small image on a blank page. The two divider pages also add bulk for very little content. A is compact and consistent across A2–A4, with images and pull quotes integrated into the text and steady section rules. A3 does have a stranded pull quote, and A1 is a plainer cover, but A reads more evenly overall.

A leaves the bottom half of page 1 and two-thirds of page 3 empty, spreading thin content across three pages. B packs the same material into two well-filled pages: the summary plus the balance sheet, then the income statement, chart and note. B's single-line title and steady flow read better. A's display font is a bit more distinctive, but its sparse pagination hurts. Both share the same reversed chart title.

A spreads thin content over seven pages. Its chapter-opener spreads (A2, A5) carry heavy side tabs. A3 and A4 are mostly empty below short text. A7 is an orphaned image on a blank page. B packs the same content into four well-filled pages (B2, B3) with consistent section rules, giving a steadier rhythm. Its only weak spot is the half-empty last page (B4). A's openers give a stronger sense of section, but the cost in empty space is too high.

B's cover carries a full-bleed illustration over a green title band, where A1 is a bare dark page. B also uses consistent header and footer bands and side-by-side pullquote panels that don't hide the images (B2, B3). A lays dark text boxes over its illustrations (A2, A3) and leaves stray fragments: an orphan paragraph at the top of A4 and an awkward big pull line on A3. A's body typography has slightly better leading, but B is more cohesive overall. B4 leaves a large empty area at the bottom.

B's cover uses a full-bleed landscape illustration over a green title band, where A's cover is a mostly empty dark page. Inside, B's text-panel-beside-image treatment is cleaner than A's dark text box laid over the illustration. B adds a running header and logo and uses consistent amber rules. A sets a larger, airier lead paragraph, but its overlaid quote boxes cover the imagery and its spacing is uneven.

A runs continuously across four pages with consistent section rules and images placed beside their text. B is inconsistent: the chapter divider pages appear only for sections 1 and 3, and B3 and B4 are left mostly empty. Section 4 has no divider and starts mid-page on B6. The orchard figure is stranded alone on a nearly blank last page (B7), separated from its text. A's only weak spot is the half-empty final page (A4), but it keeps the image beside its text.

A wastes space: half-empty pages (A3, A4), a divider page with no body (A5), and a stranded image alone on A7. Its chapter treatment is also inconsistent: dividers for chapters 1 and 3, but inline headings for 2 and 4. B flows evenly over four pages with consistent section rules, a well-integrated pull quote, and the final image paired with text (B4). B's pages are fuller and balanced.

B gives the pull quote real emphasis as a large accented line with a rule (B3), whereas A tucks it in as an indented plain line (A3). B also wraps body text beside the workshop image instead of leaving a blank column (B3 vs A3). A's solid green header and footer bands are more distinctive, and its type is slightly crisper. Overall B reads with clearer hierarchy and flow.

The two designs share the same layouts. B mixes Latin and Arabic numerals in its section numbering ("1 ملامح العام" beside "٣ الوقاية", "2" on the divider), which looks inconsistent. Its heavy dark header and footer bands also crowd the pages. A uses lighter running heads with a logo and keeps its numbering and text consistent, which gives a calmer, more refined read.

B gives each section a consistent teal band header, a running header with a logo, and a dedicated page per section. The pages read in order: the infrastructure text stays with its section instead of spilling onto the HR page as in A4. B's inset images are framed within the margins and sit better than A's full-bleed images that crowd the text. B's tables carry a highlighted current-year column and rules, which aid scanning. A's thin rules and plain headings give a weaker hierarchy. Typography is similar in both, with A slightly lighter.

A's serif body text reads well, but its divider pages are used inconsistently: only chapters 1 and 3 get one, and they waste space. A3's running header says section 2 while the page opens with the Chair's letter, and A8 is almost empty. B flows compactly with consistent ruled section headings and fuller pages, though its light sans body is slightly thin.

A's numbered section headings are larger and bolder, so the hierarchy is clearer. Its quiet cover is restrained, and the content pages read consistently. B's green header band is attractive and saves a page, but its section titles are small and light, so sections blend into body text. B also stacks gold rules over section headings, which looks busy. Both designs share the same reversed chart title and the same tables.

A uses a cleaner, more legible Arabic face. B wins on structure: numbered headings, running header and footer bands with page counts, and a large chapter number on the divider. B also starts the Prevention section on its own page (B7) instead of squeezing it under the table as A does (A6). A's TOC pages are inconsistent, with two entries both on page 6. B's pages are more consistent and easier to navigate overall.

B uses a lighter, more open Arabic text face with generous leading. A sets body text in a heavier geometric face, and its justified paragraphs on A3 and A6 produce stretched kashida-like gaps. B also adds a table of contents (B2) and numbered section headings, which strengthen navigation. One flaw in B is mixed Latin and Arabic numerals in the TOC and headings. A's text in the table caption on A5 sits cramped right under the paragraph. Charts are identical in both designs.

A is compact and consistent. Each section flows on from the last, with the chart sitting beside its numbers (A2). B spends whole pages on nearly empty section dividers (B2, B5) and strands a chart alone on a mostly blank page (B4). B's mixed body sizes also break the rhythm (B3, B6). B's serif type and cover are attractive, but the pacing is wasteful.

A opens with a full illustrated cover, sets the pull quote as a large, distinct statement, and keeps each section on its own page with generous margins. B squeezes the cover into a header band. It also splits the 'Key Figures' section across pages, leaving its stat band orphaned at the top of B2 and a large empty gap on B1. B's body text is denser and its pull quote gets lost. B's table has a highlighted current-year column, a small gain that does not outweigh these problems.

A has a strong full-bleed cover image and a large pull quote with rules, giving clear hierarchy. Its stat row is cleanly aligned. B's cover is sparse and mostly empty. B's stats misalign, with "مليون م³" wrapping and stats lacking %. Its pull quote is weak, though B has neater running headers and numbered sections. A's full-bleed images feel more editorial.

A has a coherent teal identity, a table of contents, header and footer bands, numbered sections, and a strong section divider page. Its clean sans Arabic type stays consistent with the charts. B is monochrome and has no TOC. It runs sections together mid-page with weak rule-based breaks, uses smaller headings, and gives a stark black cover. B's Naskh-style text also clashes with its Latin chart labels.

A applies a consistent teal palette with header and footer bands, larger readable sans body text, and a dedicated section divider for جودة الخدمة. Its section headings stand out clearly. B uses a small, light Naskh body with weak headings. In B, sections like جودة الخدمة and الوقاية run on at the foot of chart pages, and its stark black-and-grey charts look less finished. A has some empty lower halves, but its structure is clearer.

Design B makes better use of its pages. Its cover pairs a full-bleed illustration with a centred title band, where A's cover is an empty dark field. B places its images beside the text with the overlay panels sitting next to the art, and it closes on a balanced figure page. A has problems throughout: a caption is orphaned at the top of A4 (its image was left behind), A5 is a stranded image page that is almost entirely blank, and the overlay boxes on A2 and A3 cover most of their images. A's display face does read with some character, but B's flow and pacing are clearly stronger.

A gives every section a strong teal title band, a running header with the logo, and contained images. Its financial table highlights the current-year column. Each section opens on a clean page. B's section heads are thin rule-plus-text with weak hierarchy, and its full-bleed images are cramped. In B4 a leftover paragraph from the infrastructure section spills above the HR heading, which breaks the rhythm. B's cover is decent, but A's split cover with the logo looks more polished.

A keeps a consistent header band with a logo and gold rule, and contains images within the text margins. Each section starts on its own page, and the key-figures percentages and table percent signs are intact. B bleeds images full-width awkwardly, drops the % signs in its figures and table (B2, B5), and spills the infrastructure text onto the HR page (B4). B's cover is cleaner, but overall A reads more polished.

A opens with a strong green title band and fits the summary and balance sheet onto the first page, making a compact, well-filled two-page document. B spends a whole sparse cover page on a small centred title, then leaves large empty lower halves on B2 and B3. Both share the same reversed chart title flaw. B's numbered headings and taller chart are minor gains.

A has an illustrated cover, keeps each image with its section, and places the final orchard image beside its text on A4. B's cover is a plain dark field. Its caption source 'أرشيف البلدية' is split onto the top of B4, apart from its image. The last page, B5, is an orphaned image on an almost empty page. B's pull quote also overlays the image in a heavy dark box. A's layout flows more steadily, with consistent header and footer bands.

A fits the content onto two well-filled pages, with the KPI summary and the balance sheet sharing page 1. B leaves the lower half of B1 empty and puts the chart and note alone on B3, which is mostly blank. B's gold rules and title wrap look good, but the pagination wastes space and breaks the flow.

B has a strong illustrated cover, chapter divider pages with section navigation, consistent header/footer bands, and side-by-side image/quote panels. However, B3 and B4 leave large empty areas, and the pull quote on B6 is weakly styled. A's dense pages are more compact, and its display face looks slightly more refined. Still, A's pull quote on A4 is orphaned after the caption 'أرشيف البلدية' is split from its image, and A5 has a lone image on a mostly empty page. Its plain dark cover is also less inviting. Overall, B reads as the more polished publication.

B has the stronger identity. The teal cover band, the header bands, the gold section rules and the teal KPI band read as a deliberate report. Its table highlights the current year and has stronger rules. A's cover is nearly empty, and its stat row looks loose: the 'مليون م³' value wraps awkwardly and the stats float without containment. A does number its sections clearly and gives each section its own page, which is clean. However, B's KPI band is split from its heading onto the next page, which hurts flow somewhat.

A sets Arabic in a traditional Naskh face suited to formal report text; B's geometric Kufi-style sans reads less naturally in long Arabic paragraphs. A's full-width teal section bands give clear entry points on every page (A2–A5). A's split cover keeps the title on white, whereas B's light title sits on a busy illustration and the year wraps awkwardly onto its own line (B1). B is cleaner and more open, and it shows percentage signs that A drops (A2 vs B2). Still, A's bands and highlighted 2025 column in the table (A5) give it a more polished report feel.

B uses consistent full-width teal section bands that give the pages a clear, repeating structure. Its Naskh-style text reads more naturally than A's geometric Arabic face, which mixes clumsily with the diacritized line. B's table highlights the 2025 column. However, B's stats drop the % signs (92, 11, +6), a real flaw. A's cover is atmospheric, but B's split cover with the logo is also strong. Overall B is more polished.
